audit.title: Getting Started with Chainlink VRF V2.5
audit.summary: This is a well-structured VRF V2.5 tutorial whose biggest GEO strength is its question-phrased heading set ("How do I deploy to testnet?", "How do I test `rollDice`?"), which maps directly onto how developers query. Its biggest opportunity is machine-readability: the served page carries **no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, and no visible dates** (per measured facts), so engines get no structured trust or freshness signals. A secondary gap is the absence of a troubleshooting/error-string section and a config summary table — both are high-lift for retrieval and extraction. Honest verdict: solid, agent-usable content held back by metadata and by fragmentation of its code samples.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema + canonical + last-updated
recommendations.issue: measured facts — "JSON-LD: 0 block(s)… canonical: MISSING… dateModified absent"
recommendations.change: emit a `TechArticle` block with `headline`, `dateModified`, `programmingLanguage: Solidity`, canonical URL `https://docs.chain.link/vrf/v2-5/getting-started`, and a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-confidence and E-E-A-T for retrieval and citation.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom/error-string troubleshooting section
recommendations.issue: errors appear only inline: "the transaction will revert", `"Already rolled"`, "the callback will fail"
recommendations.change: add `## Why does my rollDice transaction revert?` and `## Why did my VRF callback fail?` sections that quote the exact revert strings and give the fix (add contract as consumer, raise `callbackGasLimit`).
recommendations.why: devs/agents query by error text; symptom-titled sections win retrieval that concept prose loses.

recommendations.title: Convert the contract-variables list into a table
recommendations.issue: six params + constraints in prose bullets; "0 table(s)" in facts
recommendations.change: a table with columns Variable · Type · Sepolia value · Constraint (e.g. `callbackGasLimit` · uint32 · 40000 · "< coordinator maxGasLimit"; `requestConfirmations` · uint16 · 3 · "≥ minimumRequestBlockConfirmations (3 on Sepolia)").
recommendations.why: tables are high-lift for extraction and let engines quote exact values per network.

recommendations.title: Lead each Q-heading section with the canonical answer
recommendations.where: "How is randomness generated…", "What is the Request and Receive cycle?"
recommendations.issue: "Randomness is very difficult to generate on blockchains."
recommendations.change: open with the liftable claim — e.g. "Chainlink VRF generates verifiable on-chain randomness using an off-chain oracle that returns a random value plus a cryptographic proof." then explain why native RNG fails.
recommendations.why: the first sentence is what engines lift; leading with the answer resists generic "use block.timestamp" priors.

recommendations.title: Provide one complete, runnable contract block
recommendations.where: end of "How can I use Chainlink VRF?"
recommendations.issue: blocks use `// ...` placeholders; identifiers `VRFD20`, `ROLL_IN_PROGRESS` never fully assembled in-page
recommendations.change: inline the full `VRFD20.sol` (with imports, pragma, all functions) in a single fenced block, not just the Remix link.
recommendations.why: agents that can't fetch Remix need one self-contained, copy-pasteable source; fragmented snippets don't run.

recommendations.title: Rename opaque link anchors
recommendations.issue: facts flag "2 link(s) with opaque text ('here', 'this')"
recommendations.change: use descriptive anchors, e.g. "create a subscription on Sepolia" / "full list of Great Houses".
recommendations.why: descriptive anchor text improves link-context extraction and citation.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers ("many, several, some") where concrete numbers are available.
Placeholder-fragmented code blocks (`// ...`, `// { constructor }`) — no single in-page block is complete.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good; confirm it lists this page.
Site-level: ensure the sitemap and canonical strategy expose the `.md` and HTML variants consistently.
Freshness cadence: a site-wide "Last updated" convention would benefit this and sibling VRF pages.
